extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners (and patent prosecutors/agents advising applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for USPTO examiners (and practitioners) on making and responding to rejections under 35 U.S.C. §§ 101, 103(b), and 112, including required form paragraphs and examples of indefiniteness, enablement, utility, and related procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability and requirements of 35 U.S.C. 103(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 103(b) applies to biotechnological processes only and makes certain otherwise nonobvious processes using or resulting in nonobvious compositions of matter be considered nonobvious if statutory conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements: (A) the biotechnological process and composition of matter must be contained in the same application or in separate applications having the same effective filing date; (B) both must be owned by or assigned to the same person at the time the process was invented; (C) a patent issued on the process must also contain claims to the composition used or made by that process, or if composition is claimed in another patent the patents must expire on the same date; (D) the process must fall within the statutory definition of 'biotechnological process' set forth in 103(b); and (E) the applicant must make a timely election to proceed under 103(b) by petition under 37 CFR 1.182 establishing satisfaction of the requirements. Timeliness: normally no later than earlier of payment of issue fee or filing of an appeal brief where a composition claim has not been rejected. If error without deceptive intent resulted in grant without an election, a reissue may permit consideration. Note: reliance on 103(b) should be rare in view of relevant Federal Circuit decisions (In re Ochiai, In re Brouwer). See 35 U.S.C. 282 for effect on presumption of validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'biotechnological process' under 35 U.S.C. 103(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of 103(b), 'biotechnological process' means specific categories of processes described in the statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: (A) processes of genetically altering or otherwise inducing single- or multi-celled organisms to (i) express an exogenous nucleotide sequence, (ii) inhibit/alter expression of an endogenous sequence, or (iii) express a physiological characteristic not naturally associated with the organism; (B) cell fusion procedures yielding a cell line expressing a specific protein (e.g., monoclonal antibody); and (C) methods of using a product produced by processes in (A) or (B) or combinations thereof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary object of examination: patentability over the prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary object of examination is to determine whether the claims are patentable over the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should concentrate effort on essential matters (prior art) and minimize undue emphasis on non-prior-art or 'technical' rejections. When a major technical rejection is proper (e.g., lack of proper disclosure, undue breadth, utility), the rejection should include a full development of reasons rather than mere conclusions or stereotyped expressions. Using form paragraphs to state rejections reduces misunderstanding as to grounds of rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraphs to state non-prior-art rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: When incorporating standard language in office actions, use the prescribed form paragraphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If language in form paragraphs is incorporated into the office action to state the rejection, there will be less chance of misunderstanding as to grounds of rejection. Refer to the specific MPEP sections for nonstatutory subject matter, Atomic Energy Act issues, duplicate claims, double patenting, new matter, foreign filing without a license, disclaimers, res judicata, reissue, and 35 U.S.C. 112 issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matter eligibility under 35 U.S.C. 101
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents are granted only for 'any new and useful process, machine, manufacture, or composition of matter, or any new and useful improvement thereof.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'process' term includes a new use of a known process, machine, manufacture, composition, or material. Examples of subject matter not patentable: printed matter (mere arrangement of printed matter), naturally occurring articles substantially unaltered (e.g., a shrimp with head and digestive tract removed), and scientific principles divorced from tangible structure. See MPEP §§ 2105 and 2106–2106.02 for microorganisms and algorithms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility requirement under 35 U.S.C. 101
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim may be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 101 for lack of patentable utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of utility includes inoperativeness, perpetual motion, frivolous, fraudulent, and public policy objections. See MPEP § 2107 for guidelines and MPEP §§ 2107.01–2107.03 for precedent. Use form paragraphs 7.04 through 7.05.03 to reject under 35 U.S.C. 101 where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.04 — Statement of Statutory Basis, 35 U.S.C. 101
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph quoting 35 U.S.C. 101 and examiner instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph must precede the first use of 35 U.S.C. 101 in all first actions on the merits and final rejections. Quote of the statute is provided; use once in a given office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.05 — Rejection heading for 35 U.S.C. 101
rubrics_metrics.description: Heading-only form paragraph for stating a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 101.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use after quoting the statute; follow this heading with one or more specific reason paragraphs (e.g., 7.05.01–7.05.03). Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.04 in first actions and final rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.05.01 — Rejection: Non-statutory subject matter (35 U.S.C. 101)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected as directed to non-statutory subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the bracket insert identification of non-statutory subject matter. Precede by 7.04 or 7.103 as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.05.02 — Rejection: Utility lacking (35 U.S.C. 101)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected because the claimed invention lacks patentable utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket provide explanation of lack of utility, e.g., frivolous, fraudulent, against public policy. See MPEP §§ 706.03(a) and 2105–2107.03. Precede as required by 7.04/7.103.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.05.03 — Rejection: Inoperative (35 U.S.C. 101)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected because the disclosed invention is inoperative and therefore lacks utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain in the bracket why the invention is inoperative. Precede as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility rejections under 35 U.S.C. 101 and 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph (¶7.05.04)
rubrics_metrics.description: A combined approach to rejecting where asserted utility is absent, not specific/substantial, or not credible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format A: use 'specific and substantial' when no asserted utility or asserted utility is not specific and substantial. Format B: use 'credible' when assessing credibility. Format C: for multiple utilities where none are specific/substantial/credible, use combined language. For any such case, also make a separate 35 U.S.C. 112 enablement rejection using Wands factors and an undue experimentation analysis (In re Wands). Treat inoperative utility as not credible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atomic Energy Act limitations on patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain inventions useful solely for utilization of special nuclear material or atomic energy in an atomic weapon are excluded from patentability under the Atomic Energy Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections 151(a),(c),(d) of the Act set limits and categorize applications that must be reported to the Department of Energy (DOE). Applications that disclose or appear to disclose atomic energy inventions are reported to DOE under 37 CFR 1.14(f) but reporting is not a determination of usefulness. All applications are screened by TC work group 3640 personnel. Rejections based on sections 151/152/155 of the Act must be made only by TC work group 3640 personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph — written description and enablement requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must contain a written description of the invention and the manner and process of making and using it in full, clear, concise, and exact terms to enable a person skilled in the art to make and use the invention and must set forth the best mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraphs 7.30.01 (quote of 112, first paragraph) and then appropriate rejection paragraphs (7.31.01–7.31.04, 7.33.01) in first actions and final rejections. The statute is only required to be recited in first actions on the merits and final rejections; otherwise use 7.103.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.31.01 — Rejection: Written description (35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected for containing subject matter not described in the specification such that it would not reasonably convey possession to one skilled in the art at the time of filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection must be preceded by form paragraph 7.30.01. In bracket identify by page/line/drawings the subject matter not properly described and explain the position, including any examiner questions not satisfactorily resolved that raise doubt as to possession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.31.02 — Rejection: Enablement (35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected as containing subject matter not enabled to allow one skilled in the art to make and/or use the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precede with 7.30.01. In bracket identify claimed subject matter lacking enablement and explain why specification is not enabling, including examiner questions not resolved. If problem is scope, use 7.31.03. Also make a separate enablement analysis per In re Wands and undue experimentation factors (MPEP §§2164–2164.08(c)). If an essential component/step is not recited, use 7.33.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.31.03 — Rejection: Scope of enablement (35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use when specification is enabling for some subject matter but does not reasonably provide enablement for the full scope of the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precede with 7.30.01. In bracket 2 identify subject matter for which specification is enabling (by reference to portions of the specification). In bracket 3 identify the subject matter for which specification is not enabling and explain why (make clear whether the deficiency is make/use/make and use). Include examiner questions not resolved. Use when claim scope is not commensurate with enabling disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.31.04 — Rejection: Best mode (35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected because the best mode contemplated by the inventor has not been disclosed; evidence of concealment may exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precede with 7.30.01. In bracket insert basis for holding best mode has been concealed (e.g., quality of disclosure effectively conceals best mode). Use of this paragraph should be rare; see MPEP §§2165–2165.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.33.01 — Essential subject matter missing from claims (enablement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected because subject matter considered critical or essential by applicant to practice the invention is missing from the claim and thus not enabled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precede with 7.30.01. In bracket recite the subject matter omitted from the claims. Examiner must cite statement/argument/date/drawing or other evidence demonstrating that applicant considered the feature essential and give rationale for omission rendering claim not enabled (see In re Mayhew).

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph — claims must particularly point out and distinctly claim
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification shall conclude with one or more claims particularly pointing out and distinctly claiming the subject matter which the applicant regards as his invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.30.02 as the statutory quotation in first actions and final rejections; otherwise use 7.103. Follow with appropriate 7.34–7.35 form paragraphs for specific defects in claim definiteness or correspondence to applicant's stated invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.34 — Failure to claim applicant's invention (35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected for failing to set forth the subject matter which applicant(s) regard as their invention, based on applicant statements outside the application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precede with 7.30.02. Identify the paper/submission (Paper No. and date) where applicant stated something inconsistent with claim scope; set forth what applicant stated and explain how that indicates the invention is different from what's claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.34.01 — Indefinite: failure to particularly point out (35 U.S.C.112, second paragraph)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected as indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter regarded as the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precede with 7.30.02. Follow with one or more of form paragraphs 7.34.02–7.34.06 as applicable. Where possible, identify the particular term(s)/limitation(s) rendering the claim indefinite and why; if the scope can be determined by one skilled in the art, this rejection is not appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.34.02 — Terminology inconsistent with accepted meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: Term in a claim used in a manner repugnant to the usual meaning renders the claim indefinite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may be his own lexicographer but cannot give a term a meaning repugnant to usual meaning. Identify the term used by applicant and the meaning assigned versus the accepted meaning. Support examiner's accepted meaning with authoritative references (textbook/dictionary). Precede with 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.34.03 — Relative term (term of degree) rendering claim indefinite
rubrics_metrics.description: A relative term of degree is indefinite where claim/specification does not provide a standard for ascertaining the requisite degree and one of ordinary skill would not be reasonably apprised of scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket explain which parameter/quantity/limitation has been rendered indefinite by the term. Precede with 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.34.04 — Broad range and narrow range/limitation in same claim
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim that recites a broad range or limitation together with a narrow range or limitation within that broad range in the same claim is indefinite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This creates ambiguity whether narrow language is exemplary or required. Insert the broader and narrower ranges and explain why ambiguity arises. Precede with 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.34.05 — Lack of antecedent basis in the claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim limitation lacks proper antecedent basis making scope indeterminate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only in aggravated situations where lack of antecedent basis makes claim scope indeterminate. Insert the limitation lacking antecedent basis and indicate where in the claim it appears. Precede with 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.34.06 — Use claims (method of using a product without steps) indefinite and possibly nonstatutory
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim directed to the use of something without setting forth the steps of the method/process is indefinite and may be an improper process claim under 35 U.S.C. 101.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert what is being used and explain lack of steps. Example: 'a method for using monoclonal antibodies of claim 4 to purify interferon' — without steps, unclear what method is encompassed. See MPEP § 2173.05(q). Precede with 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.34.07 — Claims are a literal translation
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims that appear to be literal translations into English from foreign documents and are replete with grammatical and idiomatic errors are narrative and indefinite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such claims fail to conform with U.S. practice. Precede with 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.34.08 — Indefinite language: 'for example'
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of the phrase 'for example' in a claim renders it indefinite because it is unclear whether following limitations are part of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precede with 7.34.01. See MPEP § 2173.05(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.34.09 — Indefinite language: 'or the like'
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of 'or the like' renders the claim indefinite because it includes elements not actually disclosed, making scope unascertainable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precede with 7.34.01. See MPEP § 2173.05(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.34.10 — Indefinite language: 'such as'
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of 'such as' renders a claim indefinite because it is unclear whether the limitations following the phrase are part of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precede with 7.34.01. See MPEP § 2173.05(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.34.11 — Modifier of 'means' lacks function (35 U.S.C.112, sixth paragraph considerations)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'means' clause where the words preceding 'means' do not convey a function is indefinite because equivalents cannot be determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Words preceding 'means' must convey a function (e.g., 'latch means' conveys 'latching'). If phrase cannot be restated as 'means for [function]' sensibly, it is indefinite. Cite Ex parte Klumb. Precede with 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.34.12 — Essential steps omitted (35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected for omitting essential steps, amounting to a gap between steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precede with 7.30.02. Recite omitted steps and give rationale why they are critical or essential (see MPEP § 2172.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.34.13 — Essential elements omitted (35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected for omitting essential elements, amounting to a gap between elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precede with 7.30.02. Recite omitted elements and rationale for considering them critical or essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.34.14 — Essential cooperative relationships omitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected for omitting essential structural cooperative relationships of elements, amounting to a gap in necessary structural connections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precede with 7.30.02. Recite omitted structural cooperative relationships and give rationale why they are critical/essential (see MPEP § 2172.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.34.15 — Rejection guidance for pro se applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims by pro se applicants may be narrative, replete with indefinite and functional language and fail to present complete operative devices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claim must be in one-sentence form, specify structure clearly, organized and correlated to present a complete operative device. Use when applicable. Precede with 7.30.02 or 7.103.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.35 — Omnibus type claim rejection (35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected as indefinite where it fails to point out what is included or excluded (omnibus claim).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precede with 7.30.02. Use to reject 'omnibus' claims (no further explanation necessary). Example: 'A device substantially as shown and described.' See MPEP § 1302.04(b) for cancellation upon allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.35.01 — Trademark or trade name used as claim limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim containing a trademark/trade name as a limitation fails 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, because trademarks identify source, not goods, making claim scope uncertain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert trademark/trade name and where used; specify the material/product identified or described by the trademark. Explain indefinite identification/description; cite Ex parte Simpson. Precede with 7.30.02 or 7.103.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate claims (706.03(k))
rubrics_metrics.description: When two claims are duplicates or so close that they cover the same thing despite slight wording differences, the examiner may object to the duplicate under 37 CFR 1.75.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After allowing one claim, object to the other claim as a substantial duplicate of the allowed claim. Form paragraphs 7.05.05 and 7.05.06 may be used where duplicate claims are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonelected inventions and plural claiming guidance (706.03(m))
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent is supposed to be limited to one invention or several closely related indivisible inventions, but applicants may restate the invention in a reasonable number of ways by plural claiming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts have confirmed applicant's right to plural claiming; mere difference in scope between claims can be sufficient. However, when duplicate claims are present, examiners should object as described above. Limitations on multiple inventions are handled through election/requirement practice (see broader MPEP text for procedure).
